what_this_is: The Phase 2 preregistration lock: the exact pooled (peer, anchor-event) set -- 778 customer/supplier pairs from HYP-06's own signed lock, 195 competitor pairs from HYP-07's own signed lock -- target definition, and model spec, fixed before any same-session value has been computed for any pooled pair. See 'look_ahead_disclosure' below.
what_this_is_not: Not a re-run or revision of HYP-06's or HYP-07's own already-reported results -- both remain exactly as signed and reported; this lock only reuses their already-fixed EVENT SETS for a new, differently preregistered same-session question. Not a result, not the one locked run, and not permission to compute anything. No Phase 3 authorization has been drafted, requested, or signed for HYP-08 as of this lock.

target_definition.formula: same_session_excess_return = r_peer[attributed_session] - beta * r_bench[attributed_session]. No horizon grid, no cumulation, no reference-window baseline -- the peer's benchmark-adjusted return on the EXACT trading session the anchor's own excess return is attributed to, and nothing else. See target_same_session.py's own docstring for full provenance.
target_definition.benchmark_beta_note: FIXED, never estimated -- the same anchor_shock.py AS-2 convention every prior hypothesis in this project already uses.
target_definition.horizon_grid_note: None, deliberately -- every row's own horizon field is the constant 0. This is the genuinely distinct design external review asked for: no delayed-horizon grid of any kind, unlike HYP-04/05/06/07 alike.
target_definition.return_basis: log, same as every prior hypothesis's own convention.
target_definition.residualization: NOT APPLIED, same v1 simplification as HYP-07's own target_signed.py.
target_definition.relationship_type_pooling: Every locked event carries the relationship_type its SOURCE lock already assigned (HYP-06's own customer/supplier categories, HYP-07's own competitor category), mapped by target_same_session.py to a single boolean is_competitor design column.
target_definition.sign_convention: Nothing is flipped, anywhere. A priori, economically motivated predictions, stated before any fit: customer/supplier peers POSITIVE (comovement -- shared revenue chain), competitor peers NEGATIVE (displacement, same convention HYP-07's own target_signed.py already uses). Not significant is a null either way, for either test below.
target_definition.source: target_same_session.py, hash-pinned above, first use of a same-session (no-horizon-grid) target in this project.

model_spec.estimator: CR2 clustered standard errors with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom -- clustered_se.py, reused unmodified. SIGNIFICANCE differs from every prior hypothesis: a closed-form Sidak-corrected critical t-value at k=2 EXACT preregistered tests (make_hyp08_sample_size_gate.sidak_critical_t), not a max-T permutation null -- there is no horizon grid here for a max-selection problem to exist over. See make_hyp08_sample_size_gate.py's own docstring for why this is the correct tool for this design, not a departure from this project's own discipline.
model_spec.primary_cluster_key_note: Reused unchanged from HYP-05's own re-decision (clustered_se.HYP05_TWO_WAY_LIMITATION_NOTE), a project-wide method choice, not re-decided for HYP-08.
model_spec.n_permutations_note: Not applicable -- see estimator above. No permutation null is computed for HYP-08.

test_family.test_1_primary: inference.fit_local_projections(table, horizons=(0,), cluster_key='event_id') -- the plain pooled same-session coefficient, both relationship types combined.
test_family.test_2_heterogeneity: inference.fit_interaction_model(table, cluster_key='event_id') -- the shock:is_competitor interaction coefficient.
test_family.complementarity_note: These are COMPLEMENTARY tests, not redundant ones. If the two relationship types' true effects are opposite-signed and roughly offsetting in the pooled sample, test 1 can come back null while test 2's interaction term is significant -- that is a coherent, reportable joint result, not a contradiction requiring explanation.

sample_size_disclosure.framing: EXPLORATORY -- floor is EXACT (k=2 by design), not provisional or borrowed, unlike every prior hypothesis's own floor
sample_size_disclosure.why: 973 pooled (peer, event) pairs clears the k=2-exact 152-pair floor by 6.4x. Still framed exploratory: a governance eligibility floor is not a claim of guaranteed power, and the true analyzed sample will be smaller after same-session NaN exclusion -- see make_hyp08_phase3_run.py's own real result for the actual analyzed count.

look_ahead_disclosure.already_touched: Every pooled event's anchor-side signed excess_return was already computed (HYP-04/05/06's own anchor-shock pipeline) and already used by HYP-06's and/or HYP-07's own prior, completed, spent Phase 3 runs. HYP-06's peers' MAGNITUDE-based results and HYP-07's peers' delayed-horizon signed results are both already reported and unaffected by this lock.
look_ahead_disclosure.not_touched: No same-session peer excess return of any kind, for any pooled peer around any pooled anchor event, has been computed before this lock -- target_same_session.py did not exist before this pass. This lock is written before that computation happens for the first time.

opens_no_gate: This is a computed HYP-08 Phase 2 lock, not a freeze, not a registry change, not a linkage ratification. It moves no gate condition, whatever the gate reads at the moment this file is read.
attestation_text: HYP-08's Phase 2 lock -- target definition (target_same_session.py's peer excess return on the anchor's own event-day session, no horizon grid, no cumulation), model spec, and the pooled 973-pair set (778 customer/supplier pairs reused from HYP-06's own signed lock, 195 competitor pairs reused from HYP-07's own signed lock) -- was fixed before any same-session excess return was computed for any pooled peer around any pooled anchor event. I understand this reuses two already-discovered, already-EDGAR-verified universes, not new discovery, and that it tests two preregistered questions: whether economic exposure predicts a same-session reaction at all, and whether that reaction differs between customer/supplier and competitor relationships. I understand this sample clears its own k=2-exact 152-pair floor comfortably.
